text:
incident-bot: PAGED: infra-alert-high - Elevated 5xx rate from eu-west canary nodes (alerts.redwood.net/alert/12345)
alex: acked, oncall here. jumping in. can someone paste the canary config?
samir: looks like a regional canary weight flip finished ~5m ago, 15% -> 60% eu-west. rolling out blue/green for routing change.
ops-sre: seeing 502s at the edge in eu-west, some 200s still but high tail latency. metrics: 5xx% spike 4.8% -> 18% (1m)
maria: tagging customers: payment-svc and search-svc saw errors, support ticket influx confirmed. logging shows upstream connection resets to the canary pool.
alex: immediate mitigation: thinking feature flag kill-switch to drop canary traffic back to green. can we toggle?
deploy-bot: deploy metrics: canary v2 -> accepting traffic. Rollout started by @samir at 1755554000. No automatic rollback configured.
june: @alex LD toggle handy? I can flip. which flag?
samir: flag key infra.bgw.route-eu-weight. set to 0 to cut canary. but note DNS TTL is 300 in eu-edge controller. partial clients will still hit canary for a bit.
june: doing:```sh
ldcli set infra.bgw.route-eu-weight 0 --env prod
```
june: done. new flag value propagated to control plane.
ops-sre: flag change acknowledged by control plane. routing config shows weights back to green 100% for control-plane, but edge report still shows ~22% to v2.
alex: ok edge still sending traffic. can we roll back traffic weights at global LB level?
samir: trying to decrement canary pool in envoy via admin api across eu-edge fleet. running script:```sh
for h in $(cat eu-edge-hosts.txt); do curl -sS -X POST http://$h:9901/cluster/modify -d '{"cluster": "canary-eu", "weight": 0}'; done
```
support-lead: support reporting user-facing 502s for eu customers, degrade for premium orgs too. setting priority: high.
ops-sre: envoy change applied to ~60% of hosts, but ~40% still on old config. some hosts failing due to TLS handshake mismatch while pulling new config.
maria: checking DNS — route53 shows alias for canary.euw.api -> canary-eu.lb.redwood.net with TTL 300. but external CDN caches might have longer TTL.
alex: can we reduce DNS TTL? yes, but changes take effect after 1 TTL period for cached resolvers. reduce to 30 while we heal.
samir: changing zone TTL now to 30 for canary alias. update submitted to route53 at 1755554305.
incident-bot: NOTE: owner alex (oncall) | severity: high | impact: partial region outage - eu-west canary | runbook: bluegreen-rollback.md
june: pushing a short-lived kill-switch at the CDN level to drop requests with X-Route: canary header. CDN rule pushed to edge providers via control plane.
ops-sre: CDN rule active. measured canary traffic drop from 22% -> 3% over 2 min. 5xx rate falling.
samir: still seeing ~1.2% 5xx tail on a small subset of hosts. digging into model server logs — OOM on some v2 pods due to smaller instance limits set in canary.
alex: if OOMs are the root cause, we should stop the canary entirely and scale down v2. Samir, can you scale down or cordon those nodes?
samir: scaling replica count of v2 to 0 in eu-west ASG now.```sh
kubectl scale deployment canary-v2 -n prod --replicas=0
```
samir: scaled. kube events show graceful termination, draining connections.
ops-sre: 5xx rate back to baseline ~0.4% in 4 minutes. latency normalized.
support-lead: teams notified on support slack, triage members pinged, opening a postmortem. customers with incidents: list attached in Gdoc (link).
june: TL;DR: feature flag kill switch + CDN header rule + scale down resolved immediate impact. DNS TTL reduction helped but due to external caches some clients kept hitting v2 for ~6 minutes after change.
alex: good. next steps: 1) block future canary by adding pre-deploy resource checks (memory limits); 2) ensure LB weight flips are atomic or have rollout guards; 3) lower DNS TTL during rollouts to 30 by default for canaries; 4) add automatic rollback when 5xx > 5% for 2m.
maria: assigning action items: SAMIR -> resource limits and canary pod spec audit; JUNE -> CDN kill-switch runbook + playbook; ALEX -> runbook update and follow-up postmortem; SUPPORT -> customer comms + escalations.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: resolved (mitigated) at 1755554910. duration ~9m.
alex: closing thread, will draft postmortem and link details. :thumbsup: feel free to add any missed notes.
